title: the swapper
text: A small little masterpiece. An absolute no-brainer for this amount of money. Puzzles: Every puzzle is written in a way that it doesn't require micro-managing your position, but you have to understand what steps you have to take to get to the goal. This game manages to use very little game mechanics to twist your mind in many ways. One may probably think 'what do I miss?', but you don't. You just need to think in a different way. Controls: I find this game much more playable with mouse and keyboard, but that may be a personal preference. A certain amount of speed and accuracy is required while aiming your clones, but the gamepad worked just fine (I'm just not used to it as much). Story: This is where the game really kicks in, in my opinion. The atmosphere is very unique, it feels like watching a movie while puzzling. The subject of existentiality may be a little much at some points, but I found it very well-told. The finale really gave me goosebumps.

title: the walking dead
text: Different character and unrelated story from the tv-series. This game is so rich on story and character relation that you would wish you were inside the game. Weeel if it wasn't for the human-eating hordes of zombies that seems to pop up behind every corner. At least they don't run. You play as Lee Everett - who saves a young girl, Clementine - and together they venture out to reunite Clementine with her parents, while trying to survive. Rich & deep story. Every action you take, every thing you say has an impact on future choices and how people percieve you in the story. Often you're presented with saving 1 of 2 people, who you choose and how has a huge impact on your team. - This gives a good replay-value. - At least play it through twice. Action buttons - For instance when you get attacked, you need to either press some buttons, click or rotate the mouse, choose the right dialogue choice. - Everything with a timer. This means you'll always sit on the end of your seat, adrenalin pumping. You will stay awake, just like if there was a chance a walker would break into your room while playing. The music and the atmosphere is great, and just intense like the series. You will also get attached to the characters, and that might be heartbreaking. The graphic is highly cartoonish in commendation for the comic books. It's not the best, often it looks like the layers was quickly put on eachother with no thought, but it works for this comic style. The facial expressions and mouth-movements are lagging some better details though. The DLC is a series of short stories, but with an easter egg included. No bugs or glitches experienced. However half the bad-reviews I read was about glitches and bugs, then sluggish movement. Great puzzles blended well in the game. It's also a fun little feature that the game tracks which choices the players voted, so you can see if you're mainstream or not. I was never a fast reader, sometimes had to skip-read and make a fast choice. 23£ + 5£ DLC might seem a bit expensive, but it's a game worth trying out. I bet you buy most games on discount anyway. A skip button for cutscenes would be nice after the first playthroughs. Moving around can be frustrating because it can be a bit robot-ish and because of the camera view. This would be really bad in "The Running Dead". Overall a good game. The story is worth it all. Far from Manure. The Telltale story games has become somewhat a game-genre for itself; and overwhelmingly positive is worth this game. However it is a special kind of game, so be sure you're into this sort of Puzzle-Novel-Action games before spending 23£. Best game to show to your friends, and let them figure out the controls by themselves. While you stand back and laugh at them panicking. Disclaimer - I don't have the Michonne Miniserie DLC. Also Hershel hates me.

title: the witcher 2: assassins of kings enhanced edition
text: Im really REALLY trying hard to like this game. And maybe this game will turn itself around into act II which im now in but to be honest im struggling. The countless positive reviews will point to why this game is 'great', here are some of the reasons I think it isnt: 1) The auto save system is REALLY bad. And you cant save when you like, meaning you will at times have to redo entire sections if you didnt hit F5 at that critical moment. Infuriating. Oh and you cant overwrite a save meaning I now have about 50 and counting. 2) I found the game pretty much on rails, it was not open world at all. You cant really 'do' much. You cant really 'craft' that much but oddly you can loot and collect countless items, even take objects from houses in front of their owners (hello, isnt this an RPG?), a lot that you collect is just plain junk. Its feels like the developers left something out, like there is a section to the crafting system that appears missing. 3) The game is HARD, but not in a good way. Sometimes you just repeat the same 2 spells or attacks to overwhelm an unfairly powerful enemy. And the fighting system, although more developed than Skyrim is still pretty boring. 4) The running here and there is TEDIOUS. You cant jump to any locations. Yes its pretty but its just boring after a while. 5) I found the narrative and stories EXCELLENT, ive never felt so immersed in a gameworld (apart from perhaps Bioshock series) but the gameplay didnt lend itself to the narrative at all. 6) Combat is usually hit, roll, QUERN - and repeat. Skyrim had loads of different spells, long & short range weapons. Nothing like that here. I will revisit this review while I continue the game if i feel it has redeems itself...

title: the witcher 2: assassins of kings enhanced edition
text: The Witcher series doesn't get as much mainstream attention as other RPGs like Mass Effect and The Elder Scrolls however it's slowly starting to grab hold of more and more gamers. The first title just kind of slid under the radar but this sequel really broke the ice for CD Projekt RED as evidenced by its critical acclaim and eventual debut on the PS3 and Xbox 360 consoles. The Witcher 2 has all the trappings of your typical fantasy role-playing game but what makes it stand out so much is that its world is a much darker and arguably more realistic one than other RPGs out there. The game doesn't pull any punches and shines brightest in its mature themes and content. By far the most refreshing aspect of the game is that there doesn't exist the clear-cut "good" and "evil" lines but instead events, choices, and consequences are differing shades of grey - kind of like real life.

text: Note: You do not need to have played the first game in the series to play this. Many people turn it away due to it´s poor graphic quality. I say give it a go. If you can´t stand "old style" games you will however easily get immersed into The Witcher 2. CD PROJEKT RED has brought Andrzej Sapkowski´s novels to life. I am 100% certain no other company could have done it as marvelous as they have. (Yes I have read all the books.) You are in for a real adventure with this one. If you are into linear RPG style games + Some added optional quests in each zone. The optional quests sometimes yeilds something you can always use as examples - Potion recipes, a treasure map, a book with useful information about some of the creatures you are battling or they can have some information about known characters. Then there´s the lustful side to Geralt. Sometimes you will be awarded sex with very graphic imagery and profanity. It´s a adult game so of course adult situations will occur. This is not your usual RPG -  You will come to love Geralt whether you´re a guy or a girl. The witcher 2 is a wast game with many memorable characters and monsters that you will meet on your quest to find out who the Assassins of Kings is. The game is divided into three acts each with their own unique environment. This is truly a epic game that deserves all the awards it has won. You will need to play through the game more than once (or watch a youtuber) play as in all RPG´s your decision has in impact in the world. Each decision needs to be considered as you will not know how it will impact the story ahead. One question that might seem insignificent can have a very big impact further on. I have played this game for many hours searching and discovering hidden caves with monsters or a tomb with a treasure chest. If you are not customed with this sort of game don´t go Hard mode and make yourself frustrated resulting in you not wanting to play anymore, however if you are up for a challange go ahead, there are so many magnificent encounters and I do believe playing them for the first time on Hard and not giving up will really reward you it will get your adrenaline pumping when you have just beaten a hard encounter. text: The Witcher 2 is one of the best RPGs I have ever played, and is easily the best looking. The visuals of this game are some of the best ever, and the voice acting is incredible as well. All of the music fits perfectly with the game, enhancing an already incredible experience. The first Witcher was a great game, but its successor improves in every conceivable way. The somewhat clunky combat of the first game has been made more fluid, the RPG elements have been improved even more, and the story is stronger than the first Witcher. In stark contrast to games like Skyrim, the Witcher 2 has an incredible amount of depth, with uniquely different areas of the map. While it may seem daunting to beginners, the Witcher 2's RPG mechanics are some of the best I've seen in a very long time. The Witcher 2 is an incredible game that should be in everyone's library. Even if you didn't play the first game, the Witcher 2's plot doesn't need a huge amount of backstory. I cannot recommend the Witcher 2 enough.

title: thief
text: Thief Deadly Shadows was one of the best games ever to be made, a masterpiece for the ages, so everybody had high expectations upon the fourth installment of the Thief series. To be truthfull, this game had bad reviews because it did not live to the expectations and the standards set by its predecessor. And the 10 year gap between both games, only provides more accumulation of expectations from the die-hard Garret fanbase. But in all, as a stand-alone game it is fairly good. Nice graphics and physics. Very interesting missions, with well balanced foes, and a nice array of capabilities and gadgets given to the player. The major let down was the map... A sh... Well, horrible for a game launched in 2014. Those rigid levels maps, with absolutelly no free-roaming, are suitable for a game of 2004 (like Thief III), but inadmissible for the modern gamer. Especially, since GTA and Skyrim and so forth, have settled the open-map sandbox as the pattern for and action/adventure/RPG game. The story is also a let down. They decided to reboot the series, but there are vague and incoherent references to the early time-line. So..... may centuries have passed, but the thief world is still Medievalish?? I mean, either you tottaly reboot the game, or you continue the story. That "not-meat-nor-fish" (a Portugues expression, y'all can use now) thing is the worst of both options. 3/5 2/5 (if you are a die-hard Thief franchise fan, and expect a sucessor to Deadly Shadows)

text: OK, I really don't understand the negative-lukewarm reviews of the new Thief. I'm a die-hard Thief fan, and I've been eagerly awaiting the Thief reboot for ages: this is possibly my favourite game franchise ever. That doesn't make me an impartial reviewer, but I think Square Enix has successfully retained the feel of the original Thief games, an important element of which is the variety of arrows at Garrett's disposal (using water arrows to create darkness through which Garrett can slip unseen, for example, is still a brilliant gameplay strategy), as well as Garrett's dry vocal intonation. I'm not that far in, but thus far I am very much enjoying the exploration, pickpocketing and blackjacking that made the original so captivating. As far as the comparisons to Dishonored go, I feel like perhaps I am the only gamer on the planet who thought Dishonored brought dishonor to the original Thief games it referenced. I felt profoundly disappointed by Dishonored. It felt too easy, it was unchallenging, the exploration elements were made boring by the Blink ability, and the ending was a letdown (as was the silly revenge narrative). I still think the Thief franchise - including the new one - is a better game. But perhaps I need to play it a little more first to see if my interest in the game is sustained. Nevertheless, when the reviewer for IGN complained that the arrows were 'extremely limited in where they can be used - particularly the fire, water, and rope arrows that only work on very specific objects like open-flame lights and leaking oil barrels', I did think that they missed the point. Just like in the original games, the ingenuity lies in precisely this use of the right object with the right target. At this point, I'm ignoring the haters and making up my own mind - and so far, I'm very much engrossed in the exploration and treasure-hunting, and I'm impressed with the way the game has stayed true to the originals that I loved so much.
